utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Good afternoon, everyone. Would the registrar please call the case.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. This is case number IT-98-32/1-PT, the Prosecutor versus Sredoje Lukic. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you. Well, we're here following an order made -- a decision, rather, issued on the 1st of February in relation to amendment of the indictment as a result of which it's recognised that there are new charges in the indictment that the accused now faces, and in the same decision this appearance was scheduled to give him the opportunity to tender pleas now to the indictment as amended. May I first of all take the appearances for the parties. For the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. HARMON
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. Mark Harmon and Fergal Gaynor appearing for the Prosecution. Lise-Lotte Karlsson is the case manager.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Harmon. And for the accused.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honour. I'm Djuro Cepic, Defence counsel for Mr. Sredoje Lukic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Cepic.

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Now, the amendment to the indictment is fairly clear, but because of the way parts of it are worded there are complexities that I think can only be adequately dealt with if Mr. Lukic tenders pleas afresh to every charge on which he is indicted. So --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that he's ready to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Yes. So what I propose to do, though, is in due course invite the court deputy to go through --

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: -- each of the charges in a very summarised form and to ask the accused whether he pleads guilty or not guilty, and that form will cover every one of the charges on which he appears to avoid doubt as to what his decision might be. Now, do you accept that that's the appropriate course to follow?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: And it is obviously his right if he wishes to have the whole indictment read out publicly here. Do you wish to do that or are you happy to take the indictment as read and to consent to proceeding straight to the summary of each charge and the tendering of a plea?

utterances.speaker: MR. CEPIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, I think that second option -- I think that second option is much better, much easier for all, because my client got already -- has got already indictment, Second Amended Indictment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Cepic. Now, would the registrar just read the specific element in respect of each count and invite the accused to tender his plea, in other words, to ask him whether he pleads guilty or not guilty. Mr. Lukic, could you stand, please? Each of the charges will be read to you in a summary form and you will be asked to whether you plead guilty or not guilty or you should respond to that question each time it is put to you. Do you understand that?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Carry on, please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 1, persecutions, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 8, extermination, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 9 murder a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 10, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 11, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 12, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Extermination, a crime against humanity, count 13. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 14, murder, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 15, murder, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 16, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 17, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 20, inhumane acts, a crime against humanity. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Count 21, cruel treatment, a violation of the laws or customs of war. Do you plead guilty or not guilty?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not guilty, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE BONOMY
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Lukic. You may be seated. In light of these pleas, the registrar will appoint a trial date in due course. The other consequences of the amendment of the indictment are dealt with in the decision which was filed on the 1st of February. That brings the proceedings here this afternoon to an end. Mr. Lukic, you will meanwhile remain in the custody of the Tribunal. This hearing is now adjourned.
